bullets: Most mysterious creaking noises in bicycle drivetrains are resolved by cleaning contact surfaces and tightening bolts to specified torque — a pattern observed across multiple teams using Spoke & Wrench.
Chain wear is the most reliable early indicator of when the cassette needs replacement, a key insight for proactive maintenance planning.
Frame geometry and component compatibility reveal the trade-offs inherent in design decisions, with the geometry itself signaling what compromises are being made.
Maintenance intervals for suspension systems are fundamentally risk management decisions; ignoring them leads to full rebuilds within a year.
Adopting Spoke & Wrench within a workflow makes the underlying trade-offs apparent — failure to acknowledge them results in unnecessary system overhauls.
The structural integrity of a bicycle's drivetrain depends on predictable, consistent contact points — any deviation disrupts the rider’s focus on the trail.
Linear, the ticketing system, is optimized for keyboard-driven workflows and speed — a tool that supports rapid, iterative engineering tasks.
Choosing one maintenance or design principle and testing it for two weeks enables meaningful iteration — the rest is refinement, not discovery.
